children: UK retail sales rose by 1.0% year-on-year on a like-for-like basis in September 2026, exceeding forecasts for a 0.7% gain and accelerating from 0.5% in the previous month.
Total retail sales growth also picked up to 1.3% from 0.7%, but remained below the 12-month average of 1.5%.
Food sales increased by 2.5%, while non-food sales edged up by 0.3%.
Health and beauty products recorded their strongest growth of the year, while clothing and footwear sales weakened due to unseasonably warm weather.

Separately, Barclays' measure of consumer spending rose 2.0% year-on-year, slowing from 2.1% in August. Essential spending climbed 2.5%, driven by a 17.3% jump in fuel spending as diesel prices reached record highs, while non-essential spending increased 1.8%.

Household financial confidence rose to a seven-month high of 67%, although 68% remained concerned about the upcoming budget's impact on their finances and 30% were cutting back on non-essential spending.

title: UK Retail Sales Growth Picks Up in September
